newsitem.title: UK: GKN's swift appeal softens share reaction.
newsitem.headline: GKN's swift appeal softens share reaction.

text.p: British engineering giant GKN Plc swiftly announced on Friday it would appeal a U.S. district court ruling ordering it to pay nearly $601 million for misusing advertising fees.

GKN said it expected to take its case to the US court of appeals in a month or so to appeal against what has been described as one of the biggest awards against a British company in the United States.
The group's quick decision to appeal thwarted a threatened slump in its share price on Friday.
It opened two pence lower at 972 on cautious trade, touched a low of 950 before recovering to 1008 pence by mid-morning.
"The damages were higher than anticipated but they are going to fight it," said one senior trader. "It doesn't automatically follow that they were have to pay out that much."

The U.S. district court's judgement ended a four year old litigation directly involving Meineke Discount Mufflers, GKN's U.S. exhaust retailer which has been accused of improperly taking millions of dollars for its own use from an advertising fund built up by franchisees.

The jury's award came late on Thursday, just hours after GKN reported 363.1 million pounds ($583.9 million) pretax profits for 1996, and was based on lost profits from money improperly taken from the fraud.
The award includes $591 million in punitive damages and $10 million in interests. GKN has cash reserves of 528 million pounds.
GKN said on Friday that it has been advised that it was on "very strong substantive and procedural grounds" to take its case to the U.S. court of appeals.
"It is expected that the appeal will take about 18 months to resolve," GKN said.

The group, which surprised analysts on Thursday by not making a provision for the damages in its 1996 results, quickly amended its accounts on Friday by making a provision of 270 million pounds as exceptional charges.
"This includes interest and legal costs likely to accrue pending the outcome of the appeal and will be treated as an exceptional charge in the 1996 accounts," GKN said.
The group's amended pretax, preexceptional profits now stands at 92.8 million pounds.
The jury found last month after a six-week trial that Meineke had committed fraud by taking the money in breach of contracts with franchisees.

U.S. district court judge Robert D. Potter tripled the jury's December 18 finding on compensatory damages which was put at $197 million. The original decision also had awarded another $150 million in punitive damages, now folded into the judge's award of $600.97 million.
Legal officials in the U.S. said the judgement would have far-reaching implications for franchisees and dealerships across the country.
